insights.title: Middle East conflict becomes the main drag
insights.summary: The Q4 2025 call (T1) did not discuss Middle East conflict risk. In the Q1 2026 call (T2) it became the largest guidance headwind, estimated at 100 to 125 bps of full-year global RevPAR growth. By Q2 2026 (T3), management reported Middle East RevPAR down 43% for the quarter. They also linked the region to construction delays that pushed net rooms growth toward the low end of guidance. Management noted the region is 3% of open rooms and 7% of pipeline rooms.
insights.uw_relevance: This is a new geopolitical exposure that now affects RevPAR, IMFs and unit growth guidance. Disclosures about how far conflict impacts are reflected in forward guidance may be scrutinised if results fall short.

insights.title: Net rooms growth guidance softens to low end

insights.title: Debt-funded buybacks deepen negative stockholders' equity
insights.summary: Stockholders' equity fell to -$4.53B at Q2 2026, from -$3.77B at FY2025 and -$682M at FY2023, while buybacks continued above net income (1.46x in Q2 2026, 2.25x in Q4 2025). Total debt rose from $11.87B at FY2023 to $16.91B at Q2 2026. In H1 2026, repurchases of $1,819M exceeded operating cash flow of $1,806M. Management now targets more than $4.5B of 2026 shareholder returns and has raised key-money and investment spending guidance to $1.25–$1.35 billion.
insights.uw_relevance: Repurchases above earnings while equity is negative, funded partly by new debt, are a recurring basis for creditor and shareholder challenges to board capital-allocation decisions. They also thin the balance-sheet cushion if fee growth slows.

insights.title: Debt-funded buybacks deepen negative stockholders' equity
insights.summary: Stockholders' equity was -$4.53B at Q2 2026, compared with -$3.77B at FY2025 and -$682M at FY2023. Share repurchases were $3.95B in FY2023, $3.76B in FY2024, $3.30B in FY2025 and $1.12B in Q2 2026. Buybacks were 1.46x net income in Q2 2026 and 2.25x in Q4 2025. Over the same period total debt rose from $11.87B (FY2023) to $16.91B (Q2 2026). In H1 2026, repurchases of $1,819M exceeded operating cash flow of $1,806M, with net debt issuance of $670M. Management now targets more than $4.5B of shareholder returns in 2026.
insights.uw_relevance: Repurchasing shares in excess of earnings while equity is negative, funded partly by new debt, is a recurring source of creditor and shareholder scrutiny of board capital-allocation decisions. It also reduces balance-sheet cushion if conditions weaken.

insights.title: Hotel owner group letter signals owner friction
insights.summary: On the Q2 2026 call an analyst asked for a public response to a letter from a group of hotel owners. The CEO declined to respond publicly and said meetings with that group are ongoing. Management has cut loyalty charge-out rates by roughly 5% and is introducing an intent-to-recommend (ITR) incentive. The ITR incentive reimburses up to 50 basis points of gross room revenue fees and will be paid by Marriott, not the system fund. The 10-K risk factors say owner disagreements rise when hotel returns weaken and have resulted in arbitration or litigation. The board also raised its co-brand credit card royalty rate after amending a long-standing contractual limit.
insights.uw_relevance: Organized owner discontent in an asset-light model can turn into contract disputes, arbitration or litigation over system fund and loyalty economics. Concessions are already being absorbed in Marriott's own P&L.

followups.question: What is the plan and timing for refinancing the $4.5B revolving credit facility that expires December 14, 2027, and how much headroom does the company currently have under the 4.5x maximum leverage covenant?

followups.uw_relevance: Liquidity stress or a covenant issue would heighten scrutiny of prior capital-return decisions by directors and officers.

followups.question: What specific issues does the hotel owner group's letter raise, what is the status of the ongoing meetings, and has any owner initiated or threatened arbitration or litigation over system fund, loyalty or fee economics?
followups.summary: On the Q2 2026 call the CEO declined to publicly respond to a letter from a group of hotel owners and said meetings are ongoing. Marriott has cut loyalty charge-out rates by roughly 5% and introduced an ITR incentive of up to 50 bps of gross room revenue paid by Marriott.
followups.uw_relevance: Organized owner discontent in an asset-light model can escalate into contract disputes or claims alleging mismanagement of system fund and loyalty economics.

followups.question: What is the property-related dispute behind the $27M litigation accrual recorded in Q2 2026, is any further loss reasonably possible, and are other similar claims pending?
followups.summary: A $27M property-related litigation accrual was a main reason owned, leased and other net fell to $49M from $78M a year earlier. Full-year guidance for this line was cut on each call, from $230–$240 million to $175–$185 million.
followups.uw_relevance: An accrual large enough to be called out in results, with the underlying dispute undescribed, is direct litigation-exposure information, and repeated guidance cuts raise disclosure-credibility questions.

followups.question: What assumptions about the Middle East conflict are embedded in current full-year 2026 RevPAR and fee guidance, given that Q4 is the region's peak quarter?
followups.summary: Systemwide Middle East & Africa RevPAR fell 33.1% in Q2 2026, with Middle East RevPAR down 43%. In Q1 2026 management estimated the drag on full-year global RevPAR growth at 100 to 125 bps.
followups.uw_relevance: If results fall short, statements on how far conflict impacts were reflected in forward guidance may be scrutinised in securities claims.

followups.question: Why has management shifted from point guidance on 2026 net rooms growth to emphasizing a 30-month CAGR of 5.2%, and how many pipeline rooms are affected by construction delays in the Middle East?
followups.summary: Net rooms growth language moved from expecting acceleration to 4.5%–5% to 'more likely to be towards the low end' of that range. The Middle East accounts for 3% of open rooms and 7% of pipeline rooms.
followups.uw_relevance: Unit growth is a core investor KPI, and softening point guidance is a signal that can underpin disclosure-based claims if targets are missed.

followups.question: What process did the board and audit committee follow in amending the long-standing contractual limitation and raising the share of co-brand card payments recognized as royalty, and has any owner challenged the allocation?
followups.summary: Marriott raised its card royalty recognition after amending a contractual limitation, and later disclosed a 26% royalty rate with $100M–$125M of uplift expected by full-year 2028 from new Chase and American Express agreements. Management initially declined to size the increase.
followups.uw_relevance: A management-determined split between loyalty program funding and Marriott royalty could draw owner or regulatory challenge, and initially vague disclosure is a disclosure-quality point.

followups.question: What is the subject of the material definitive agreement 8-K flagged on 2026-09-24, and does it affect debt, card economics or owner arrangements?

followups.question: How has the CFO transition from Kathleen Oberg to Jennifer Mason been managed for SOX certifications and the Development function she also led, and have any control deficiencies been identified during the reservations, property management and loyalty platform migration?

followups.uw_relevance: A new principal financial officer certifying financials during a major systems migration raises the risk of control deficiencies and restatement-related claims.

followups.question: Who now leads the US & Canada segment following William P. Brown's departure effective March 28, 2026, and what change in board status did director Debra L. Lee report, including the effect on Inclusion and Social Impact Committee leadership?

followups.uw_relevance: Simultaneous changes in the CFO, largest-region leadership and board committee composition affect oversight continuity.

followups.question: How does the board monitor compliance with the 2024 FTC and state attorney general Starwood breach settlements, and have any assessments found gaps that could trigger enforcement or contempt proceedings?
followups.summary: The 2018 Starwood breach led to 2024 settlements with the FTC and attorneys general of 49 states plus DC imposing long-term data-privacy and security requirements. followups.uw_relevance: Ongoing consent obligations create continuing board oversight duties, and noncompliance could lead to enforcement and derivative claims.

followups.question: What return thresholds and board approval limits govern key money commitments now that 2026 investment spending guidance has risen to $1.25–$1.35 billion, and what clawback protections exist if owners default?
followups.summary: In T1 the CFO guided 2026 investment spending of $1 billion to $1.1 billion; by T3 the CEO called key money 'the weapon of choice' and guidance rose to $1.25–$1.35 billion. Total debt reached $16.91B at Q2 2026.
followups.uw_relevance: Rising key money alongside debt-funded shareholder returns increases balance-sheet sensitivity if fee growth slows or owners fail.

followups.question: How much of the higher-than-typical technology transformation spending is expected to be reimbursed by owners, over what period, and how is that reimbursement being received in light of the owner group letter?
followups.summary: Capital and technology spending includes higher than typical transformation costs that management expects owners to reimburse over time. Separately, a group of hotel owners sent a letter to which the CEO declined to respond publicly.
followups.uw_relevance: Contested owner reimbursement could combine systems-related cost overruns with owner disputes, increasing claims exposure.

followups.question: What triggered the $68M impairment on a US & Canada hotel in Q2 2026, are other owned or leased hotels under impairment review, and how were the Sonder exit charges treated in adjusted versus GAAP results?
followups.summary: Q2 2026 included a $68M impairment with a $17M related tax benefit in H1, and Sonder's November 2025 exit produced one-time charges including $23M in owned, leased and other results excluded from adjusted figures. Reported Q4 2025 net income was $445M and EBITDA $954M.
